chapter: Rose Murphy, wartime 52nd Street, Town Hall
title: Touring with Rose Murphy, the Chi-Chi girl
summary: Murphy sang in a very high voice; they toured the country as a duo and with a drummer, and made an album, for about two years from the mid-'50s.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Okay, let us go. Now we stopped off, you were telling me about a pianist that you worked with for a few years, a female pianist named Chi-Chi.
And did you travel much -- did you travel a lot with her?

I traveled quite a bit with her and of course, I did mention that once in a while we did a duo and on other occasions, we had an added drummer with us. We traveled all across the country and like I think I mentioned, we had the beautiful opportunity of going to Australia and it was quite a nice set-up there. We even made an album of a few numbers and it was real nice, you know. She used to -- I don't

know if you remember, but she was famous for that high voice that she used to sing in the high register there along with her piano playing. She wrote a few tunes. Of course, one of the tunes that she really featured was "I Can't Give You Anything But Love." You probably remember that. And with her high voice, it was very unique and enjoyable to work with her for -- I'd say on and off for about two years.
When did you first work with her?
That was back in -- oh, let's see, about the mid-'50s.
